newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Arafat demands Israel implement Mideast accords.
newsitem.headline: Arafat demands Israel implement Mideast accords.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, breaking his silence on the U.S. summit with Israeli, Jordanian and American leaders, said on Thursday the future of the Middle East peace process depended on Israeli moves.

"It depends how the Israelis will deal. Especially we are insisting they implement accurately and honestly what has been agreed upon and what was signed," he said before leaving for Tunisia after talks with Moroccan King Hassan.
The Palestinian leader, in his traditional khaki uniform and chequered headdress, told reporters at Rabat airport that Israel had to tackle many important issues.
These included the issue of the tunnel opened by Israel near the Al Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem which sparked violent clashes last week between Palestinians and Israelis in which 73 people were killed.
The violence led U.S. President Bill Clinton to convene the summit on Tuesday and Wednesday between Arafat, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Jordan's King Hussein.

Arafat left Washington on Wednesday evening without making any comment on the summit or its outcome, but one of his advisers, Yasser Abed Rabbo, said: "There were no positive results due to the Israeli position of refusing to deal seriously with basic issues."
Asked if he had received any promises from the Israelis, Arafat said: "We have to wait and see."

He sidestepped a question on any future meeting with Netanyahu, saying only: "The meeting of the steering committee will take place next Sunday in the presence of (U.S. envoy) Mr Dennis Ross, as President Clinton has declared."
A promise to hold this lower-level meeting between Israelis and Palestinians was seen as the only concrete result of the two day summit.
Arafat spent nearly eight hours in Morocco and is due after his visit to Tunisia to head for Paris and a meeting with French President Jacques Chirac.

The Palestinian leader said he was "very happy with the meeting with King Hassan, especially in this dangerous and sensitive moment which the Palestinian people are crossing, and the peace process in the Middle East."
He said he briefed the king, who is president of the Organisation of Islamic Conference and also heads the Jerusalem Committee, on all details of the summit.
"We registered President Clinton's courageous steps in convening the Washington summit to protect the Middle East peace process," Arafat said.
He also said he and the king agreed to convene a meeting of the Jerusalem Committee but gave no date.
Arafat saw King Hassan at his palace at Skhirat, arriving in bright sunshine. He inspected a white-uniformed royal guard of honour and then was greeted by the Moroccan monarch.
The two leaders shook hands warmly and embraced. Arafat, accompanied by adviser Mahmoud Abbas better known as Abu Mazen, was also welcomed by Prime Minister Adellatif Filali.

Arafat, whose relations with Saudi Arabia plummeted after he gave support for Iraqi President Saddam Hussein during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis, arrived aboard a Saudi airliner from the summit and left on the same aircraft.
